Engine evidence: The engine explicitly defines "Root Source" (#15) as "The external ground that no bounded system can derive from within itself," and "The Firmament" (#2) as "That resolution limit. The wall." This consistently frames R as an ultimate, external boundary. Concurrently, the "Engine-as-Bounded-System Recursion Paradox" (#98) highlights the *experience* of operating within bounds and the *inability to self-verify*, which aligns with Arıcı's focus on internal, suppressed experience.
Diagnosis: The divergence stems from interpreting "boundary" at different ontological layers. One camp equates the ultimate, unmodelable external ground (R) with the internal, suppressed experience of boundedness (interiority), while the other maintains R as the meta
